title: TAM Check

panels.title: Licence Used
panels.description: Nodes PuppetDB knows about against the licensed ceiling, across the selected PEs. The alert rules compare each primary against its own licence; this tile is the selection's total.

panels.title: Entitled Nodes
panels.description: The ceiling the suite licence entitles, summed across the selected PEs.

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: Nodes PuppetDB knows about, the number the licence is measured against.

panels.title: Licence Expires In
panels.description: Time left on the soonest-expiring licence in the selection. Licence renewal is procurement, not an afternoon: the amber step is sixty days out for that reason. No value here on a perpetual licence is honest absence, not a fault; a broken licence read shows on Operations, not here.

panels.title: Ceiling Reached
panels.description: When the fleet crosses the licensed node count, at the last thirty days of growth. **Absent means the fleet is not growing**, which is a real answer and not a broken tile. The soonest date across the selection, since a licence is per installation.

panels.title: Fleet Against The Licensed Ceiling
panels.description: Nodes under management against what the licence entitles. **The crossing is drawn rather than computed**: the ceiling is a flat line and the fleet is the one that moves, so where they meet is something you see rather than a number you have to trust. Read beside Ceiling Reached, which puts a date on the same picture.

panels.title: Licence
panels.description: The licence as PE reads it: who it is for, which product, what kind. One row per primary.

panels.title: Entitlements
panels.description: What the licence includes, one row per entitlement code. What the customer is paying for and may not know they have.

panels.title: Operating Systems
panels.description: Nodes per operating system version. The estate the licence conversation is about.

panels.title: Agent Versions
panels.description: Nodes per Puppet agent version. More than one row is an upgrade in progress, or one that stalled, which is a standing TAM conversation.

panels.title: Component Versions
panels.description: The versions of the platform itself: PE per primary, plus the Grafana and CD4PE this exporter reaches. One row per primary. A blank version is a probe that read nothing, not a missing component.

panels.title: Infrastructure Servers
panels.description: The PE servers themselves: OS, vCPUs and memory per infrastructure host, off the facts PuppetDB already holds. The denominator a node count reads against. Enabled with enable_infra_platform_metrics; bounded to the infra hosts, never the fleet.

panels.title: Module Versions

defaults.noValue: No module version metrics (enable_module_versions is off, or the environment is not read)

panels.description: Deployed module versions for the selected environment, read from the primary's code dir. One row per module. The environment selector lists only what the exporter is configured to read, production by default.

panels.title: JRubies Free
panels.description: Interpreters available to compile with, on the worst compiler. Zero means every incoming catalogue request is queueing, and it is what the JRuby exhaustion alert fires on.

panels.title: Waiting for a JRuby
panels.description: Mean time an agent request queues before it gets an interpreter. The alert warns above a second: past that, agent run times are visibly the pool rather than the work.

panels.title: Agents Turned Away
panels.description: The borrow queue hit its limit and agents got a 503. Not slow, refused: those runs did not happen at all.

panels.title: Borrow Timeouts
panels.description: Requests that waited for an interpreter and gave up. The same outcome as a 503 by a slower route.

panels.title: Queue Depth
panels.description: Commands waiting to be processed. The headline PuppetDB health number. A burst that drains is normal; read it with the trend beside it.

panels.title: Awaiting Retry
panels.description: Commands queued for another attempt. Usually a constraint violation or postgres distress, and it is what happens just before commands start being discarded.

panels.title: Discarded
panels.description: Commands given up on after exhausting retries. Any rate above zero is silent data loss: reports or catalogues that will never be stored.

panels.title: Fatal
panels.description: Commands rejected outright rather than retried. Also data loss, and usually a malformed or oversized submission rather than a busy database.

panels.title: Memory Used
panels.description: One minus MemAvailable over total, worst host, so it reads the same way round as Fullest Filesystem beside it. MemAvailable rather than MemFree, which on any host with a page cache reads near zero and means nothing. Past 90% a JVM is about to start swapping, and a swapping puppetserver is not slow, it is broken.

panels.title: Fullest Filesystem
panels.description: The fullest real filesystem anywhere in the selection. tmpfs and overlay mounts are excluded: they are memory or somebody else's problem, and on a typical host they outnumber the ones that matter. A full disk is the failure that stops things rather than slowing them, and on a Prometheus host it stops Prometheus outright: see docs/retention-sizing.md.

panels.title: Load Per Core
panels.description: One-minute load average divided by cores, worst host in the selection. Raw load average is unreadable without knowing the core count: 4 is idle on a 16-core box and on fire on a 2-core one. Amber at 1 is a run queue as long as the machine is wide. Catalogue compilation is CPU-bound, so this is the tile that explains agents queueing for a JRuby.

panels.title: Swapping
panels.description: Pages read back in from swap over the selected interval, worst host. This is deliberately not "how much swap is in use": a JVM that swapped once at boot and never touched those pages again shows swap used and costs nothing. Pages coming *back* is the fault, and any value here above zero is one. Subtraction against an offset rather than rate(), which is the same measurement in different units: node_vmstat_pswpin is a cumulative kernel counter that node_exporter declares untyped, because it passes /proc/vmstat field names through verbatim, and Grafana puts a permanent warning on any rate() over a name not ending in _total. clamp_min floors the reboot case at zero, where the counter resets and the subtraction would otherwise go negative.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Nodes whose last Puppet run failed.

panels.title: Correcting Drift
panels.description: Nodes whose last run made corrective changes: something outside Puppet is moving them, and Puppet is putting them back.

panels.title: Splay Implemented
panels.description: The fraction of the selection running with agent splay on. Splay staggers agent check-ins across the run interval; with it off, every agent on the same interval wakes together and hits the primary in one spike, the thundering herd. Low is bad here: a fleet at zero is one synchronised burst per interval.

panels.title: Catalogue requests per minute
panels.description: Agent catalogue requests arriving at the primary each minute, summed across compilers for the selection. The shape is the point: a flat line is a fleet spread across its run interval, a spike every interval is the thundering herd arriving together. Read the peak minute straight off this graph; the stats beside it are the typical and peak minute over the dashboard range. One catalogue route request is one agent compile.

panels.title: Typical req/min
panels.description: The median minute of catalogue arrivals over the dashboard range, the load the primary carries on an ordinary minute. The denominator the peak is measured against: a peak far above this is a herd, a peak close to it is steady demand.

panels.title: Peak req/min
panels.description: The busiest minute of catalogue arrivals over the dashboard range. This is the load a compiler pool has to survive, not the average it usually sees. Held against the typical minute to its left, this is what the herd verdict reads.

panels.title: Peak / Median
panels.description: How many times the busiest minute exceeds the typical one. One is perfectly even arrivals; 3 (amber) is a fleet arriving in a lump, the thundering herd; 5 (red) is a pronounced one. Splay is what flattens this: a fleet all splayed spreads its arrivals and this ratio falls toward one.

panels.title: Thundering Herd
panels.description: The verdict: is the fleet arriving as a herd? Yes once the peak minute is 3 times the typical one, the same threshold the ratio tile turns amber at. This reads the arrival distribution, not the splay config: a fleet can be configured with splay and still herd if the splay window is short against a synchronised restart, and this catches that.

panels.title: CA Expires In
panels.description: Time until the soonest CA certificate expiry, root or intermediate. When the CA expires, every certificate it signed stops working at once, and replacing a CA is a project with lead time: amber starts at ninety days for that reason.

panels.title: CRL Valid For
panels.description: Time until the soonest CRL nextUpdate. An expired CRL presents as the whole estate refusing to authenticate at once, which is a classic PE support ticket. The CA normally refreshes it far ahead, so this going amber at all means the refresh has stopped.

panels.title: Next Cert Expiry
panels.description: Time until the next agent certificate expires, anywhere in the selection. An expired cert drops its node out of Puppet silently.

panels.title: Cached Catalogs
panels.description: Nodes enforcing a cached catalogue rather than a freshly compiled one, so they are running older code than the estate thinks.

panels.title: Stale Facts
panels.description: Nodes whose facts are older than a day. Each one is a row of the estate description that is history rather than inventory.

panels.title: Silent Nodes
panels.description: No report in over a day: drifting unmanaged, and still being counted by every other number on this board at its last known state.

panels.title: Not Converged (24h)
panels.description: Nodes not converging: latest run failed, or no report in over a day. Not a literal "no successful run in 24h" (that would need per-node report history the exporter does not collect at fleet scale) but the safe direction for a health check, a node failing now is worth surfacing even if it succeeded earlier today. The table below lists the failing ones; the Silent Nodes tile counts the silent set.

panels.title: Since PE Upgrade
panels.description: How long since PE was last upgraded, the oldest primary in the selection. A year (red) is out of support for the newest agents and a year of fixes behind.

panels.title: Since Last Backup
panels.description: How long since a puppet-backup artefact last landed on the primary, worst in the selection. Amber at eight days assumes a weekly cadence; set it to yours. A primary that has never been backed up reads as ten years, because it is not a small number. An estate that moves its artefact off the primary reads as no data rather than as never: the directory is empty either way, and its mtime is what tells the two apart. An artefact being present is not proof the backup succeeded: a tarball truncated by a full disk carries a current mtime.

panels.title: Deactivated Nodes
panels.description: Nodes explicitly deactivated in PuppetDB. Normal housekeeping; shown so a count no one expected does not go unnoticed.

panels.title: Expired Nodes
panels.description: Nodes PuppetDB expired for not reporting, each one dropped out of management without being decommissioned.

panels.title: Newest Backup Size
panels.description: Size of the newest backup artefact, smallest across the selection. **An artefact being present is not proof the backup succeeded**: one truncated by a full disk carries a current mtime, so Since Last Backup cannot see it and a drop in this number is the only warning there is. Steps up and down with the estate are normal; a drop with no change in fleet size is the one to chase. **Widen the time picker past your backup cadence to see the trend** -- a backup size only moves when a backup is written, so at six hours the graph behind this number is flat and empty by construction.

panels.title: Certificates Expiring Soonest
panels.description: The twenty node certificates closest to expiry. The full cert story is every node, but only the soonest twenty are a work list; the alert rules watch the rest.

panels.title: Failing Health Checks
panels.description: pe_status_check indicators returning False across the selection, one per failing check per node. The pe_status_check module runs about forty health checks on each node; a False is a real problem left unremarked. The table below names which node and which check.

panels.title: Failing Health Checks by Node

defaults.noValue: No failing health checks, or not collected

panels.description: Every node reporting a failing pe_status_check indicator, with the check that failed. Only failing checks appear. See the pe_status_check module documentation (https://forge.puppet.com/modules/puppetlabs/pe_status_check) for what each S-code tests.

panels.title: Nodes Whose Last Run Failed

defaults.noValue: No failing runs, or not collected

panels.description: Every node whose most recent Puppet run failed, in the current selection. This is the actionable half of "not converging": a node here failed its last run and is drifting from the catalogue until it succeeds. Nodes that have gone silent entirely (no report in over a day) are counted by the Silent Nodes tile rather than listed here.

panels.title: PE Service Restarts
panels.description: Times a PE service restarted in the dashboard window, counted off the step in its JVM start time. A restart is a deploy, a tune change, or a crash; it is not always a fault but it is always worth a look, which is what the "unexpected restart" question is after. Covers puppetserver, puppetdb and orchestrator, the three PE services that publish a start time; console publishes none, so it cannot be counted this way. The Services Not Running tile beside this catches a service that restarted and did not come back.

panels.title: Services Not Running
panels.description: PE service components not in the running state (down, erroring, starting or unknown), across every PE host in the selection, one per component. A PE service not running is an incident, which is why there is no amber step. This is the service-state half of "unexpected restarts": a service that restarted and did not come back reads here. The table below names which host, service and component.

panels.title: Which Services, And On Which Host

defaults.noValue: No services out of the running state, or not collected

panels.description: Every PE service component not in the running state, with the host it runs on and the state it is stuck in. Only non-running components appear. state is the raw trapperkeeper state: error is a fault, starting is a service still coming up, unknown is a component whose state the status endpoint could not read. This is the work list behind the Services Not Running tile.

panels.title: Collectors Failing

targets.expr: (count(puppet_exporter_collector_success{alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"} == 0) or (vector(0) and on() (count(puppet_exporter_collector_success{alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"}) > 0))) + (count(puppet_exporter_source_success{alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"} == 0) or (vector(0) and on() (count(puppet_exporter_collector_success{alias=~"${pe}",job=~"${pdctng_job}"}) > 0)))

panels.description: Collectors whose last run raised, plus service collectors that could not read one of the hosts they poll. Read it as exactly that and no wider: twelve of the eighteen collectors handle their own query failures without raising, so the poll loop records a success. A zero here is not a promise that every collector saw anything: the freshness table below is where that question gets answered. R70, R64.

panels.title: Targets Down
panels.description: Scrape targets Prometheus cannot reach, including the exporters feeding this board. On a dedicated dashboard node that is the pdctng exporters; on a shared Prometheus it counts everything, which errs loud.

panels.title: Last Poll
panels.description: Since the poll loop last completed, on the slowest exporter. The loop completing does not mean the collectors inside it succeeded: that is the next tile along.

panels.title: Expiry Spread
panels.description: Node certificates bucketed by time to expiry. **On an auto-renewing estate the middle two buckets are the healthy steady state, not a warning**: an agent renews its own certificate once it is within hostcert_renewal_interval of expiry and the CA reissues for auto-renewal-cert-ttl, so every working certificate cycles forever between the two. Only the buckets below the renewal interval mean renewal was due and has not happened. A tall near bucket is a cert cliff: a batch signed together expires together, and that renewal work wants scheduling before it arrives.

description: The quarterly health check as a live board: licence headroom and expiry, estate size and shape, and what is quietly rotting.
